title: Public Health payments to nonprofits per person in mental-health or substance-use care
question: How much did Public Health pay nonprofits for each person who received a mental-health or substance-use service?
finding: Per person receiving a mental-health or substance-use service: $5,008 in 2020 and $7,264 in 2025 (+45%), as the money went from $267.4 million to $387.3 million (+45%) and the count from 53,406 to 53,317 (-0%).
how: Money: Public Health payments to nonprofits in the fiscal year, leaving out the University of California. Count: the department's yearly figure for people who received a mental-health service plus people who received a substance-use service in the City's health network and its contractors; a person who received both is counted twice.
limits: This is the loosest ratio in the set and is shown because no closer one can be built from public data. The money covers every Public Health nonprofit contract, including HIV, primary care and housing services, while the count includes people seen in City-run clinics; payment data does not separate behavioural-health contracts. The count is the department's own. The money is everything the department paid nonprofits that year, so this is the cost of the whole system set against one result, not the price of that result: most of the money keeps people housed, sheltered or in care who are not counted as a new result. A falling count can reflect harder cases or fewer openings rather than weaker work, and the pandemic distorted 2020 to 2022.
